Las fracciones equivalentes del tema de: The equivalent fractions of the fractions topic had one property: the cross products agree. That detail, applied to real-world quantities —kilos and euros, workers and days— is the whole of proportionality. The topic then adds percentages, which are fractions with denominator 100, and ends with interest, which is a percentage applied many times over.
Una <strong>razón</strong> entre dos can: A ratio between two quantities is their quotient: $\frac{a}{b}$. A proportion is the equality of two ratios. And out of that comes the most used tool in all of school mathematics: the rule of three.

It reads: “a over b equals c over d if and only if a times d equals b times c”.

A rule of three is exactly this with one of the four quantities unknown: if 3 kg cost 6 €, how much do 5 kg cost? You write $\frac{3}{6} = \frac{5}{x}$, multiply crosswise, $3x = 30$, and out comes $x = 10$.
Dos magnitudes son <strong>directamente: Two quantities are directly proportional if multiplying one by a number leaves the other multiplied by the same number. The quotient between them is constant: that constant is called the constant of proportionality.
Son <strong>inversamente proporcionales<: They are inversely proportional if multiplying one by a number leaves the other divided by it. Now what is constant is the product.
Antes de aplicar ninguna regla, pregúnta: Before applying any rule, ask yourself: if one quantity increases, does the other increase or decrease? More kilos of fruit, more money → direct. More workers, less time → inverse. Getting this wrong is getting the whole problem wrong.

El interés compuesto es la razón de que: Compound interest is why a 30-year mortgage costs far more than the money lent, and why a deferred credit card is so expensive: 20 % a year does not mean paying 20 % more, because interest earns interest. The same formula, seen the other way round, is what explains why starting to save ten years earlier changes the outcome more than saving twice as much. When you get to exponentials you will see it is the same curve.
El interés compuesto es más antiguo que: Compound interest is older than almost everything else in this course: there are Babylonian tablets from almost four thousand years ago working out how long a lent capital takes to double, and the answer they give matches the one a calculator would give today. For centuries, however, charging interest was forbidden or frowned upon in Christianity and Islam, and much of medieval financial engineering consisted of inventing contracts that did the same thing without calling it that.
